styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny folding stool with a purple cushion and gold X-frame legs, much smaller than one 16x16 tile. Its measured tones per tile are 0, and it has only 13 distinct colours in total, so the numbers say little. By eye the cushion is a near-flat purple block with a single highlight band and a simple dark base. The gold legs have about 2-3 steps and no grain, wear marks or per-part shading. The references (well, stall, hedge) show 5-6 steps per material, plus tile scallops, clustered foliage and stone-by-stone shading. The candidate's dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted (dark purple and dark brown-gold) and not black. The shading is still shallow, and the cushion and legs read as flat fills. Even next to the simple bench, it looks thinner and more sticker-like. The bench also has more wood grain and more separation between slats.
